_note: L2040 SEASON BIRD TABLE — DRAFT (owner OK pending; no prompt edits, 0 gens). Research: web search found NO canonical 'one bird per season' set in Chinese embroidery; only 喜鹊登梅 (magpie + plum) is firmly attested as a fixed motif (bird of joy + flower of spring). The pairs below are built from classical seasonal imagery (poetry: 燕/黄莺 spring, 荷塘鸳鸯/翠鸟 summer, 雁/鹤 autumn migration + 秋词, 喜鹊+梅 winter) = a design convention, not a museum canon. Sources checked: chinasage.info/symbols/birds, theworldofchinese birds-and-their-meanings, Nelson-Atkins four-seasons flower-and-bird embroidery (no species named).

ranks.t5-t6: ONE small pair of birds, picked from the season's list, small & clear (F13 spirit: not cluttered)
ranks.t7-t8: phoenix is the only bird (I3); no season birds on t7/t8 or triều phục
ranks.never: no phoenix on t1-t6; season birds never long-tailed or gold-multicolour (phoenix look); never on maids' sleeves/skirts (keep maid ranks simple)

colour_logic: Same tone logic as F20. Plumage body = the embroidery-flower colour of that outfit (flower_colours_L2013.json embroidery_hex) so bird and flower belong together; one small accent (beak/breast/cheek) from the species' natural hue CLAMPED to the outfit's tone class (soft outfit → pale accent); gold-thread outline on every bird; bird never darker than the robe pattern around it and never the main robe colour. Winter/dark robes: bird lighter than robe, as flowers.
